Code trace confirms the sibling/bind inconsistency and the misleading-message outcome.

(1) No upstream normalization: serve() lines 557-559 take host from `--host` (Click, verbatim) or `_load_toml_server_host` which returns the TOML string verbatim (`return host`, line 143, no strip), then builds `ServeConfig(host=host, ...)` with no strip/validation. handle_serve line 524 -> _abort_if_port_in_use line 321 -> `_port_is_available(config.host, config.port)` passes the raw host through.

(3) `_port_is_available` (lines 182-194): line 182 `family = _socket_family_for_host(host)` strips internally so a padded `" 127.0.0.1 "` correctly yields AF_INET and the socket is created; but line 191 `probe.bind((host, port))` uses the RAW host. For an AF_INET socket CPython routes a non-numeric-literal host string through getaddrinfo; a whitespace-padded numeric string fails the inet_pton fast path and getaddrinfo rejects it, raising socket.gaierror (a subclass of OSError). Lines 192-193 `except OSError: return False` collapse that resolution failure into the same `False` value used for EADDRINUSE.

The sibling-vs-bind inconsistency itself is incontrovertible from the code; the misleading message is the standard consequence. No guard exists upstream (no host validation at CLI or ServeConfig layer).
verdict.recommended_fix: Normalize the host once at the source — strip in serve() (line 558) or in ServeConfig — so every consumer, including bind, sees the canonical value; this alone removes the inconsistency.
